case.caseTitle: Driver injured in vehicle roll-over on delivery run (practice copy)
case.location: Remote delivery route, 40 km from the Area Production Centre
case.initialDescription: A driver delivering goods to a remote location left the Area Production Centre on schedule at 08:00 and was due back at 12:30. His failure to return was not reported until 15:00. A search along his Journey Management route started at 16:30 without success; he was found off the designated route at 18:30. The vehicle had left the road and rolled over. Local villagers had pulled the driver from the vehicle while he waited for rescue; doctors believe this contributed to a spinal injury that will probably cause permanent disability.
case.refinedDescription: Five trios describe the incident, from the need to transport goods to the permanent disability of the driver. Seven barriers failed. The Tripod causation paths point to weaknesses in journey management, driver fitness and rest control, driver training, seat-belt enforcement and emergency response staffing.

rootCause.immediateCauses: Journey manager misses opportunity to combine loads; Journey manager does not stop non-rested driver; Driver fades on and off behind the wheel; Driver over-steers vehicle; Driver refuses to wear seatbelt; Emergency team mobilises after 75 minutes; Search team makes detour before finding crashed vehicle

keyLearnings.text: Journey management must cover driver fitness and rest, not only the route.
Urgency on transport requisitions should be challenged and loads combined.
Seat-belt use is a company rule regardless of local law and must be enforced from induction onwards.

correctiveActions.finding: Addresses Failed Barrier: Combining load with other loads
correctiveActions.action: Logistics planners to check delivery urgency with the requester before dispatch and combine non-urgent loads with scheduled truck runs.

correctiveActions.finding: Addresses Failed Barrier: Stop non-rested driver to drive
correctiveActions.action: Add a documented driver fitness and rest check to the journey management pre-departure briefing; Journey Manager to stop any driver who fails it.

correctiveActions.finding: Addresses Failed Barrier: Alert and correct steering
correctiveActions.action: Brief every driver before departure on fatigue: when drowsy, pull off and take a 20-minute nap. Record the briefing on the Journey Management Plan.

correctiveActions.finding: Addresses Failed Barrier: Correct reaction on hitting shoulder of road
correctiveActions.action: Add recovery from running off the road (slow down, steer back gently) to the practical module of the advanced driving course.
Require the planned route to be written on the Journey Management Plan and any deviation to be reported to base before it is taken.

correctiveActions.finding: Addresses Failed Barrier: Use of seatbelt
correctiveActions.action: Make seat-belt use a stated condition of driving company vehicles and check it at gate exits for three months.

correctiveActions.finding: Addresses Failed Barrier: Rapid mobilisation of search team
correctiveActions.action: Rehearse overdue-vehicle search mobilisation against the 45-minute target at random times, quarterly.

correctiveActions.finding: Addresses Underlying Cause: Inadequate communication about urgency of the delivery
correctiveActions.action: Agree delivery priority definitions with customers and hold a monthly delivery planning meeting.

correctiveActions.finding: Addresses Underlying Cause: Fitness of drivers is no issue in journey management procedure
correctiveActions.action: Revise the Journey Management Procedure to include driver fitness, rest and alertness criteria.

correctiveActions.finding: Addresses Underlying Cause: Resting is not controlled; drivers are on call
correctiveActions.action: Introduce duty-hour and minimum-rest rules for drivers and monitor them through the roster.

correctiveActions.finding: Addresses Underlying Cause: Too few drivers on this job
correctiveActions.action: Review driver numbers against trip demand and recruit or reschedule to remove the shortfall.

correctiveActions.finding: Addresses Underlying Cause: Company does not require advanced driving course
correctiveActions.action: Require an advanced driving course (alertness, fatigue and vehicle recovery skills) for all drivers.

correctiveActions.finding: Addresses Underlying Cause: Management does not enforce use of seatbelts
correctiveActions.action: Correct the induction material on seat belts and brief all induction trainers on the company rule.

correctiveActions.finding: Addresses Underlying Cause: Local culture stimulates "macho driving"
correctiveActions.action: Run a line-manager-led driving culture programme with recognition for compliant driving and visible follow-up of risk-taking.

correctiveActions.finding: Addresses Underlying Cause: Management does not enforce duty procedures
correctiveActions.action: Audit compliance with emergency duty and on-call procedures monthly and report results to the management team.

correctiveActions.finding: Addresses Underlying Cause: Shortage of operators due to cost-cutting drive
correctiveActions.action: Remove outdoor duties from control-room operators while on emergency watch, or add a relief operator.

correctiveActions.finding: Addresses Underlying Cause: Ineffective tracking system for road transport
correctiveActions.action: Fit in-vehicle tracking to field vehicles and monitor positions from the control room.
